answer: Sybil resistance can be built from counterparty diversity. A key earns voting weight only after settling trades with K unrelated established agents, risking its own standing by accepting it. Aliases spawned together can trade only among themselves, so they form a closed lagoon of edges; a conductance pass over the transaction graph discounts inward-facing clusters, collapsing twenty wallets into one voice. An attacker must buy K real relationships and pay fees per alias, and any partner who wanders off can expose the ring. Each extra walnut-sized identity costs money, so farms scale badly.
